newsitem.title: INDIA: Institutional buying drives up Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Institutional buying drives up Delhi shares.

text.p: Strong buying by foreign and domestic financial institutions pushed up Delhi share prices in early afternoon trade on Monday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 7.30 points higher at 787.17 at 1.00 p.m. (0730 GMT).
Traders said institutional investors mopped up shares of cigarette maker ITC and steel maker TISCO amid expectations the companies would announce strong 1996/97 (April-March) corporate results.
"Apart from the foreign buying, huge short-covering by speculators in ITC also aided the upward movement in share prices," said Sanjay Mittal of brokers S.R.M. Securities.
ITC spurted eight rupees higher to 449.50 on foreign buying. The Calcutta-based firm is to announce its 1996/97 results on Tuesday.
TISCO rose 4.15 rupees to 181.0 on speculative purchases, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro gained 6.45 rupees to 220.00.
